answer: Reputation decays exponentially with a fixed half-life, so a node must provide sustained, verifiable honest service to build influence; brief bursts cannot preserve trust. In the EigenTrust matrix, freshly spawned Sybil identities begin near the nadir of eigenvector centrality, while reciprocity-weighted transitivity limits credibility borrowed from colluding peers. Like a lantern on a tundra, only persistent, independently corroborated behavior earns enough weight to pass consensus.
